name: Atlanta district (St. Joseph Lead Co. boom mill heads)
quote: During the recent boom, the mill heads averaged slightly less than 0.5 ounce of gold per ton and from 1 to 2 ounces in silver.

name: Atlanta lode (early shipping ore, pre-1876)
quote: Much of the ore mined prior to 1876 was rich enough to stand shipment by pack train and wagon to the railroad 230 miles away and by rail to smelters in Omaha end New Jersey. The value of many of these shipments averaged more than $700 a ton, some as much as $2,000 and small lots as much as $11,000.

name: Boise-Rochester mine (1932 mill heads)
quote: The St. Joseph lead Company sought to maintain an average mili head of 0-5 ource of gold per tone During 1932, the assay value of the 51,5457 tons of ore . mined was 0.4614 oz. of gold and 1.4885 oz. of silver per tone

name: Boise-Rochester mine (1935 stoping ore, largely Monarch ground)
quote: The 57,637.1 tons of stoping ore, . in large part from Monarch ground, had an assay value of 0.382 oz. of gold per . ton and 1.038 oz. of silver.

tonnage: crosscut average across full 30-ft width; plus $1.40/ton in silver
name: Monarch mine (No. 2 level crosscut, 1902-1910 reopening)
quote: On the Noe 2 level, the ore body was reported to be from 10 to 30 oo feet wide, and in one of the crosscuts averaged $20.80 in gold and $1.40 in silver : for the entire width of 30 feet. (Price based on $20.67 gold.)

name: Monarch mine (earliest shipping ore)
quote: Some of the earliest ore mined was excéptionally rich and netted as much as $800 a ton even after the costly haul to Kelton, Utah, and shipment to New Jersey . and to Omaha smelters

tonnage: 1,701 tons milled 1881; $56,101.36 Au / 1,701 t = $32.98/t; bullion also carried $113,456.30 in silver; separate 151-ton smelter lot netted $114,654
name: Buffalo mine (1881 mill run, gold content)
quote: It is reported that 151 tons shipped to Omaha netted bullion worth $114,654, 4 whereas,in 1881, 1,701 tons of ore treated in the Buffalo mill yielded 102,378 ‘ ounces of bullion, containing $56,101,36 in gold and $113,456.30 in silver

tonnage: silver comprised two-thirds of gross value of Buffalo production
name: Buffalo mine (mill-ore tenor)
quote: It is difficult to estimate the tenor of the ore mined. Some of the bonanza pockets near the surface are reported to have contained ore assaying $8,000 to t he tone That treated in the mill assayed from $100 to $800 to the ton.

name: Last Chance mine (early mill ore)
quote: The ore was clearly of the bonanza type, Ore milled in the early days is ree ported to have yielded $100 per ton, half of which was in free gold, 20 to 30 per cent in sulphide concentrates, and the balance in silver.

name: Minerva mine (1905 ore)
quote: In 1905, the ore is reported to have assayed about one ounce of gold per ton, more than 60 per cent of which was saved by amalgamation.

name: Minerva mine (uniform-grade ore bodies)
quote: It is also reported that there are large bodies of fairly uniform grade, much of which assayed about $14 to the ton in gold and silver, The gold was exceptionally free.

tonnage: 300 tons treated in the Buffalo mill, 1881
name: Tahoma mine (1881 mill lot)
quote: Prior to 1883, ore from the Tahoma was treated in the Buffalo mill. It is reported that,in 1881, 300 tons of ore yielded $100 to $150 per tore

name: Tahoma mine (average tenor)
quote: Although some of the ore treated in the Buffalo mill yielded from $100 to $150 per ton in gold and silver, the average tenor is reported to have been $50 to $100 per ton.

name: Big Lode (Leonora) mine
quote: The ore first mined was reported to be rich, but at a depth of 60 feet the lode is reported to have increased in size. The gold and silver were thus more widely dispersed and the tenor of the ore correspondingly diminished. Be lyaey assays showed the ore to run about $15 a ton in silver and about $8 in gold.

tonnage: 100 tons treated by the Buffalo mill in 1883
name: Jessie Benton mine (1883 mill lot)
quote: Some of the ore mined in the early days was high-grade for 100 tons of ore treated by the Buffalo mill in 1883 was worth $123,53 per ton.

name: Washington mine (rich ore layer)
quote: The Yashington is reported to be from 2 to 22 feet thick, but the richer ore was in a layer 12 to 18 inches wide which assayed about $40 in gold.

tonnage: mill heads also averaged 1.7 per cent cobalt
anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: Uncle Sam mine (mill heads, 1940-41)
quote: At the Uncle Sam mine the mill heads averaged 1.7 per cent cobalt and about the same amount was retained in the goldecopper concentrate shipped to the smelter. The mill heads also averaged about 0.22 eunce of gold per ton and 4.5 per cent copper.

tonnage: 563 tons of ore and concentrates shipped to Anaconda, 1939-41 (mixed crude ore + concentrates, not crude ore alone)
anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: Uncle Sam mine (ore and concentrates shipped to smelter)
quote: Ore and concentrates shipped to the suelter averaged 0.665 ounee in gold and 0e51 ounce in silver per ton.

tonnage: bottom-level shaft body reputed 0.8 oz Au, up to 18% Cu, 2% Co
anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: Brown Bear mine
quote: According to old reports, some of the ore at the Brown Bear carried 2 to 3 per cent copper, some cobalt and nickel, and about 0,075 ounce of gold per tone A body cut by the Brown Bear shaft and a cross-cut on the bottom level is reputed to have carried 0.8 ounce in gold, up to 18 per cent oopper, and 2 per cent cobalt.

anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: St. Joe mine (pyrrhotite body)
quote: Hess records that a body of pyrrhotite 6 feet thick is reported to have been cut at a depth of 100 feet and again at 250 feet. This ore is said to have carried nearly an ounce of gold as well as some cobalt and nickel

anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: Bryan-Columbus prospect (gossan)
quote: The gossan is reported to carry about 0.12 ounces in gold. Grab samples from the old dump are reported to show 0.10 per cent cobalt.

tonnage: copper and cobalt percentages OCR-garbled ('546 per cent copper, 1,9 per cent sobalt')
anchor_hint: Blackbird Creek, WSW of Salmon, Lemhi Co.
name: Tom Jefferson prospect
quote: An analysis of some of to have shovm 0,2 owes of gold per ton, 546 per cent copper, and. 1,9 per cent sobalt,
